doc: Geometry at and above the routed-stream input pins of every inverter master. Where-is-the-metal only: no cause claim, no fix claim, no openness verdict -- openness is the committed open_pin_probe.json connectivity record's to say. Instance enumeration is the stream's own SREF order per master (klt-extract's `master_N` names are a different, non-contractual numbering); master-level binding to the connectivity findings is by master identity.

provenance.layer_table_source: gf180mcu.map (libs.tech/klayout/tech), recorded as the LAYERS table in this script; presence verified in the stream

notes: The LEF I-pin RECT set (what the router may connect to) and the GDS labelled M1 cluster (what extraction treats as the pin) are different sets for the wide inverters: the first LEF rect carries no label and is M1-disconnected from the label cluster in the flattened stream, joining it only through the cell's transistor gates.
A trace that stops at a layer describes the metal present, not an open: only the connectivity record decides openness.
PDN strap overlap is measured from the stream's own M4/M5 shapes (>= 4 um across), not from the request; routed wires on those layers are narrower.
